title: ThreadPoolExecutor — all 7 parameters, queue-full behavior, four rejection policies

s1_definition.profdef: `ThreadPoolExecutor` is the most configurable thread pool with 7 constructor parameters: (1) **corePoolSize** — minimum workers (always alive, even idle). (2) **maximumPoolSize** — max workers under burst load. (3) **keepAliveTime + unit** — idle time before non-core workers die. (4) **workQueue** — `BlockingQueue` where tasks wait when all core workers are busy. (5) **threadFactory** — creates worker threads (set names, daemon status). (6) **rejectionHandler** — what to do when queue is FULL and max workers reached. **Task flow**: submit → workers < core? Create new worker. Workers ≥ core? Queue task. Queue full? Workers < max? Create non-core worker. Workers = max AND queue full? → REJECTION HANDLER fires. Four policies: `AbortPolicy` (throw exception — default), `CallerRunsPolicy` (caller thread executes — back-pressure!), `DiscardPolicy` (silently drop), `DiscardOldestPolicy` (drop oldest queued task).
s1_definition.analogy: **Core workers** = 5 permanent tellers (always on duty). **Max workers** = 10 (5 extra can be called during rush). **Queue** = waiting line with 100 spots. **keepAlive** = extra tellers go home after 60 seconds of no customers. **threadFactory** = HR hiring policy (name badges, department). **When line is full + all 10 tellers busy**: `AbortPolicy` = "SORRY, COME BACK LATER!" (reject). `CallerRunsPolicy` = manager serves the customer themselves (back-pressure). `DiscardPolicy` = customer silently turned away (dangerous!). `DiscardOldestPolicy` = kick out the person who's been waiting longest, serve the new one.
s1_definition.oneliner: 7 params: core, max, keepAlive, queue, factory, handler. Flow: core → queue → max → reject. AbortPolicy (exception), CallerRunsPolicy (back-pressure), DiscardPolicy (silent drop), DiscardOldestPolicy (drop oldest).
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** `ThreadPoolExecutor` is the most configurable thread pool with 7 constructor parameters: (1) **corePoolSize** — minimum workers (always alive, even idle). (2) **maximumPoolSize** — max workers under burst load. (3) **keepAliveTime + unit** — idle time before non-core workers die. (4) **workQueue** — `BlockingQueue` where tasks wait when all core workers are busy. (5) **threadFactory** — creates worker threads (set names, daemon status). (6) **rejectionHandler** — what to do when queue is FULL and max workers reached. **Task flow**: submit → workers < core? Create new worker. Workers ≥ core? Queue task. Queue full? Workers < max? Create non-core worker. Workers = max AND queue full? → REJECTION HANDLER fires. Four policies: `AbortPolicy` (throw exception — default), `CallerRunsPolicy` (caller thread executes — back-pressure!), `DiscardPolicy` (silently drop), `DiscardOldestPolicy` (drop oldest queued task).

**In simple words (banking analogy):** **Core workers** = 5 permanent tellers (always on duty). **Max workers** = 10 (5 extra can be called during rush). **Queue** = waiting line with 100 spots. **keepAlive** = extra tellers go home after 60 seconds of no customers. **threadFactory** = HR hiring policy (name badges, department). **When line is full + all 10 tellers busy**: `AbortPolicy` = "SORRY, COME BACK LATER!" (reject). `CallerRunsPolicy` = manager serves the customer themselves (back-pressure). `DiscardPolicy` = customer silently turned away (dangerous!). `DiscardOldestPolicy` = kick out the person who's been waiting longest, serve the new one.

**One line to remember:** 7 params: core, max, keepAlive, queue, factory, handler. Flow: core → queue → max → reject. AbortPolicy (exception), CallerRunsPolicy (back-pressure), DiscardPolicy (silent drop), DiscardOldestPolicy (drop oldest).

sections.s3_banking: **Problem — The payment service used `Executors.newFixedThreadPool(10)` — unbounded queue!** During payment gateway outage: tasks piled up (each blocked 30s on timeout). 1000 req/s × 30s = 30,000 queued tasks × ~1KB each = 30MB → 300MB → OOM after 10 minutes. Fix: `ThreadPoolExecutor(10, 20, 60s, LinkedBlockingQueue(500), namedFactory, CallerRunsPolicy)`. Queue capped at 500. Beyond: CallerRunsPolicy → HTTP thread executes payment itself → slows down Tomcat → natural back-pressure → client sees latency increase instead of OOM crash.

sections.s5_journey:
**Step 1.** Pool: core=2, max=4, queue=3. Submit task-1 → worker-1 created (workers < core). Submit task-2 → worker-2 created.

**Step 2.** Submit tasks 3-5 → workers ≥ core → queued (queue: 3/3).

**Step 3.** Submit task-6 → queue FULL → workers < max → worker-3 created. Submit task-7 → worker-4 created.

**Step 4.** Submit task-8 → queue FULL + workers = max(4) → REJECTION HANDLER fires!

**Step 5.** After burst: workers 3-4 idle for 60s → keepAlive expires → workers die → back to 2 (core).
sections.s5b_flow:
```
  ═══ TASK SUBMISSION FLOW ═══

  submit(task)
    │
    ├── workers < corePoolSize(5)?  → YES → CREATE core worker!
    │
    ├── NO → queue.offer(task)
    │         ├── queue accepts?    → YES → QUEUED! Wait for free worker.
    │         │
    │         ├── NO (queue FULL!)
    │              ├── workers < maxPoolSize(10)? → YES → CREATE non-core worker!
    │              │
    │              └── NO (max reached!) → REJECTION HANDLER!
    │                   ├── AbortPolicy:        throw RejectedExecutionException!
    │                   ├── CallerRunsPolicy:   caller executes task! (back-pressure)
    │                   ├── DiscardPolicy:      silently drop! (dangerous!)
    │                   └── DiscardOldestPolicy: drop oldest queued, retry new!

  ═══ keepAliveTime ═══
  Non-core workers idle > 60s → die → pool shrinks back to core!
```
sections.s5c_hld:
```
  ═══ HLD — Production Payment Pool Config ═══

  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Payment Service                                   │
  │                                                    │
  │  ThreadPoolExecutor:                              │
  │  core=10, max=20, keepAlive=60s                   │
  │  queue=LinkedBlockingQueue(500) ← BOUNDED!        │
  │  factory="payment-worker-N" ← NAMED!              │
  │  reject=CallerRunsPolicy ← BACK-PRESSURE!        │
  │                                                    │
  │  Normal: 10 workers + queue absorbs bursts        │
  │  Burst:  up to 20 workers + 500 queued            │
  │  Overload: CallerRuns → Tomcat thread slows down  │
  │  After burst: extra workers die after 60s idle    │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
sections.s5d_lld:
```
  ═══ LLD — ThreadPoolExecutor 7 Parameters ═══

  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  ThreadPoolExecutor(                      │
  │    int corePoolSize,      // min workers  │  always alive
  │    int maximumPoolSize,   // max workers  │  burst capacity
  │    long keepAliveTime,    // idle timeout │  non-core die
  │    TimeUnit unit,         // time unit    │
  │    BlockingQueue<Runnable> workQueue,     │  task buffer
  │    ThreadFactory threadFactory,           │  create workers
  │    RejectedExecutionHandler handler       │  queue full!
  │  )                                        │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────┘

  ┌─ Rejection Policies ─────────────────────┐
  │  AbortPolicy:        throw REE! (default)│
  │  CallerRunsPolicy:   caller executes!    │  BEST for back-pressure!
  │  DiscardPolicy:      silent drop!        │  DANGEROUS!
  │  DiscardOldestPolicy: drop oldest, retry │
  │  Custom:             (r, e) -> log(r)    │  log + alert!
  └──────────────────────────────────────────┘

  PRODUCTION RULES:
  (Recommended) BOUNDED queue (LinkedBlockingQueue(N))
  (Recommended) Named threads (threadFactory)
  (Recommended) CallerRunsPolicy or custom rejection
  (Avoid) UNBOUNDED queue (OOM risk!)
  (Avoid) Executors.newFixedThreadPool (unbounded queue!)
  (Avoid) DiscardPolicy (silent data loss!)
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
ThreadPoolExecutor has 7 parameters: corePoolSize (minimum workers), maximumPoolSize (burst capacity), keepAliveTime (idle non-core workers die), workQueue (bounded task buffer), threadFactory (named workers), and rejectionHandler (what to do when full). Task flow: workers < core → create. Workers ≥ core → queue. Queue full + workers < max → create non-core. Queue full + workers = max → REJECT.

Four rejection policies: AbortPolicy (default — throws RejectedExecutionException), CallerRunsPolicy (BEST — calling thread executes the task, creating natural back-pressure), DiscardPolicy (silently drops — DANGEROUS), DiscardOldestPolicy (drops oldest queued). In production: ALWAYS use bounded queues (unbounded → OOM), named threads (debugging), and CallerRunsPolicy (or custom logging handler). NEVER use `Executors.newFixedThreadPool()` in production — its unbounded queue can OOM. In banking: payment pool with CallerRunsPolicy — gateway outage → queue fills → Tomcat threads execute payments themselves → request latency increases → clients see slowdown instead of OOM crash.

---

keyPoints: Queue + max determines when rejection happens
